result: Backend tests/build and TypeScript checks pass, but source inspection found malformed integer defaults are not rejected. Vite build separately blocked by EPERM.

evidence.outcome: TypeScript noEmit passed with exit code 0.
Blocked separately: EPERM writing node_modules/.vite-temp; source checks were not implicated.
Discovery covers selected version, space-age content, enabled mods, catalog fingerprint, save basename/hash, and enabled mod name/version/hash compatibility.
Schema, unknown-key, wrapper, typed-value, enum, numeric-range, and RGBA validation is fail-closed.
Mod-settings API enforces authorization, CSRF, owner/admin mutation access, explicit stopped confirmation, and 409 when running.
Startup fails closed for missing, invalid, or stale artifacts and atomically materializes the PropertyTree input with header, flag, nested sections, typed values, colors, and empty sections.
Artifact persistence is temporary-file based with replacement and backup handling.
Defect: integer default parser uses -?\d+\b and accepts the numeric prefix of malformed values such as default_value = 1.2, so malformed int defaults are silently accepted as 1 instead of rejected.

Regression tests cover typed validation, enum/range rejection, color key/range rejection, malformed/missing defaults, wrapper null/missing values, schema rejection, and malformed definitions, but not malformed integer token prefixes.

next_slice.summary: Fix default and numeric-bound parsing to require a complete valid token for the declared type, add regression coverage for malformed integer defaults such as 1.2, then rerun backend and frontend checks.

blockers: Vite build could not run because the bundled Vite process received EPERM writing node_modules/.vite-temp; TypeScript noEmit passed.
